name: Course Plans and Graduation Audits
title: Course Plans and Graduation Audits
answer: Course plans and graduation audits use AI tools to help students choose courses that keep college, career, and trade options open, and to catch missing credits before graduation. The counselor reviews and approves every plan and every audit flag, because records can be wrong and because a tool's suggestions can quietly limit a student's ambitions. The point is to protect a student's future choices while keeping a person accountable for the decisions.

sections.body: Course selection has long term consequences, so a four year plan needs to include the courses that keep college, careers, and trades within reach. AI tools in platforms such as Scoir and BigFuture can help students explore courses that match their interests and goals. Graduation audits work the same way, with student information systems flagging missing credits or requirements so problems surface early. The idea solves two problems at once, the risk of a student drifting through school without the right courses and the risk of a graduation surprise late in senior year. Catching a problem in junior year leaves time to fix it.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: In practice, students use the platform to explore course options, then a counselor reviews and approves the plan. Student information systems run graduation audits that flag missing credits or requirements, and a counselor reviews each flag because records can contain errors or miss courses taken elsewhere. Career and technical education and dual credit pathways let students earn industry credentials or college credit while still in high school, and AI can help counselors map these pathways and explain them clearly to students and families. The text does not give separate grade band guidance, though it notes that catching a problem in junior year leaves time to fix it. The counselor makes sure each student's plan meets graduation requirements and fits their goals.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The text gives no study, figure, or finding for this idea, and it carries no evidence label. It rests on practice rather than research, describing how platforms such as Scoir and BigFuture and student information systems are used, and what counselors do with what those tools produce.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: Plans must reflect the student's own interests and potential, not assumptions. A tool that suggests courses based on past grades might steer a student away from a challenge they could meet, so counselors should encourage students to aim high. Counselors should also watch for patterns in which groups of students are placed in advanced courses, and the algebra placement discussion in Chapter 7 applies here too. The counselor reviews and approves every plan and reviews each audit flag, since records can contain errors or miss courses taken elsewhere. The decisions stay with the counselor and the student, not with the tool.
